title: Highest-Protein Vegetables: How Much They Actually Provide

seo.title: Highest-Protein Vegetables per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Compare Brussels sprouts, artichokes, kale, spinach and broccoli by protein per 100 grams and serving, with context versus legumes and meat.
seo.search_intent: Compare vegetables by protein without overstating their contribution.

excerpt: The highest-protein common vegetables usually provide about 2.5–4 g per 100 g. They contribute protein, but far less than legumes, tofu, eggs, fish or meat.
content_html:
Vegetables contain protein, but they are not protein foods in the same sense as legumes, tofu, eggs, fish or meat. The higher-protein vegetables generally provide around 2.5–4 g per 100 g.

Higher-protein vegetables

VegetableProtein/100 g
Cooked Brussels sprouts~3.4 g
Cooked artichoke~3.3 g
Cooked spinach~3.0 g
Cooked kale~2.9 g
Cooked broccoli~2.4–3.0 g
Cooked asparagus~2.4 g
Cooked cauliflower~1.8 g

Protein in a serving

A 150 g serving of Brussels sprouts provides about 5 g protein; 150 g broccoli about 4 g. The same weight of cooked lentils provides roughly 13.5 g and cooked chicken breast about 46.5 g.

Peas and edamame

Cooked green peas provide around 5.4 g/100 g and edamame about 11–12 g. Both are legumes, even though they are often served alongside vegetables.

Broccoli and protein per calorie

Broccoli has about 35 calories and 2.5–3 g protein/100 g, equivalent to roughly 7–8 g protein per 100 calories. Chicken breast is around 18.8 g per 100 calories and lentils around 7.8 g.

Broccoli therefore looks respectable per calorie, but getting 20 g protein would require roughly 700–800 g of broccoli.

What vegetables contribute beyond protein

Vegetables supply fiber, folate, vitamins C and K, carotenoids and potassium in varying amounts. Their nutritional importance does not depend on being a major protein source.

How to make a vegetable meal higher in protein

Pair vegetables with legumes, tofu, eggs, fish, dairy or meat. Two hundred grams of broccoli supplies about 5 g protein; adding 6 ounces / 170 g firm tofu can bring the meal into the 25–30 g range depending on the tofu.

Bottom line

Brussels sprouts, artichokes, spinach, kale and broccoli are among the higher-protein vegetables, but their serving-level contribution is modest. When a meal needs substantial protein, vegetables work best alongside a dedicated protein source.

Sources

Values come from USDA FoodData Central.

faq.question: Which vegetable has the most protein?
faq.answer: Brussels sprouts, artichokes and cooked spinach are around 3–3.5 g/100 g among common vegetables.

faq.question: Is broccoli high in protein?
faq.answer: It provides about 2.5–3 g/100 g, or roughly 4 g in a 150 g serving.

faq.question: Is edamame a vegetable?
faq.answer: It is young soy and botanically a legume, with about 11–12 g protein/100 g.
